'''Alexandre Tkatchenko''' (born 1980) is a professor of theoretical chemical physics at the [[University of Luxembourg]] who works in [[intermolecular interactions]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tkatchenko |first=Alexandre |last2=Scheffler |first2=Matthias |date=2009-02-20 |title=Accurate Molecular Van Der Waals Interactions from Ground-State Electron Density and Free-Atom Reference Data |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.073005 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en-US |volume=102 |issue=7 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.073005 |issn=0031-9007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251230213441/https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.073005 |archive-date=2025-12-30 |doi-access=free |access-date=2026-01-23 |url-status=live |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0010-F9F2-D |hdl-access=free }}</ref> [[chemical physics]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Theoretical Chemical Physics |url=https://tcpunilu.com/ |access-date=2026-01-23 |website=tcpunilu.com |language=en}}</ref> and [[materials physics]]. He serves as Head of the Department of Physics and Materials Science. Tkatchenko is a 2019 recipient of an [[American Physical Society]] Fellowship, in the Division of [[Computational physics|Computational Physics]], cited "''For the development of a novel framework for modeling and understanding [[van der Waals interactions]] in molecules and materials''".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019 |title=APS Fellowship recipients |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=Alexandre%20Tkatchenko&af=true |access-date=23 Jan 2019 |website=APS Fellows Archive}}</ref>

== Education ==
Tkatchenko earned a bachelor's degree in computer science, and a Ph.D. in physical chemistry, with the thesis "[https://bindani.izt.uam.mx/concern/tesiuams/8623hx862 Estudio del potential atomo-superficie y su influencia sobre la estructura de monocapas adsorbidas]" ("Study of atom-surface potential and its influence on the structure of adsorbed monolayers") at the [[Universidad Autónoma Metropolitana]] in [[Mexico City]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexandre TKATCHENKO - CV |url=https://www.uni.lu/fstm-en/people/alexandre-tkatchenko/ |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=FSTM EN |language=en-GB}}</ref> From 2008−2010, he was an [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]] at the [[Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society]] in [[Berlin]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards - Surface Science {{!}} ScienceDirect.com by Elsevier |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/surface-science/about/awards/recognizing-emerging-talent-in-surface-science-15-years-of-gerhard-ertl-young-investigator-and-best-paper-awards |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=www.sciencedirect.com}}</ref> where he led an independent research group from 2011–2016.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Alexandre Tkatchenko Biography, ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1012-4854 |access-date=2026-01-24 |website=orcid.org}}</ref>

Tkatchenko serves on the editorial boards of ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'' (APS) and ''[[Science Advances]]'' (AAAS).<ref name=":0" /> He was elected [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society (2011–present)|Fellow of the American Physical Society in 2019]], and has earned the 2020 [https://www.watoc.net/watoc.dirac.html Watoc Dirac Medal]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Watoc Dirac - medal |url=https://www.watoc.net/watoc.dirac.html |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=www.watoc.net}}</ref> from the [[World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists]], the 2011 Gerhard Ertl Young Investigator Award of the [[German Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wegkamp |first=Daniel |title=Department of Physical Chemistry - FHI Berlin - MPG |url=https://pc.fhi-berlin.mpg.de/gerhard-ertl/gerhard-ertl-young-investigator-award/ |access-date=2026-01-25}}</ref> and grants from the [[European Research Council]]: a Starting Grant in 2011,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2011_stg_results_all_domains.pdf|title=ERC Starting Grants 2011 Results|page=5}}</ref> a Consolidator Grant in 2017,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Uni.lu Professor Awarded ERC Grant to Develop Chemical Discovery Platform|url=http://www.chronicle.lu/category/research-r-d/35144-uni-lu-professor-awarded-erc-grant-to-develop-novel-chemical-discovery-platform|website=Chronicle.lu|access-date=2026-01-23}}</ref> a Proof of Concept Grant for his project MACHINE-DRUG,<ref>{{Cite web|title=ERC Grant for Prof. Tkatchenko to speed up drug development with AI|url=https://www.uni.lu/en/news/erc-grant-for-prof-tkatchenko-to-speed-up-drug-development-with-ai/|website=UNI EN|access-date=2026-01-23|language=en-GB}}</ref> and an ERC Advanced Grant on Quantum Materials in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ERC Advanced Grant on Quantum Materials for Prof. Alexandre Tkatchenko|url=https://www.uni.lu/en/news/erc-advanced-grant-on-quantum-materials-for-prof-alexandre-tkatchenko/|website=UNI EN|access-date=2026-01-23|language=en-GB}}</ref>
